method: Comparative desk triage of existing report summaries, modeled native outcomes, cost boundaries, missing inputs and relevant resource passages. No original-source revalidation or numerical recalibration in this screen. This planning pass is not forty-five completed research reports or forty-five minutes of research; no fabricated per-organization intervals were assigned.
timingPolicy: Focused income-materiality checks capped at60seconds per organization, counted within (not added to) the existing300second combined initial allowance when report-specific research begins. Only in-depth reviews receive900seconds. No padded waits.
threshold: 90% health share requires a defensible upper bound on positive income-equivalent welfare below healthQALYs/9, for the same attributed cohort, counterfactual, horizon and cost window. Signed losses must be checked separately: apparent health dominance does not excuse material taxes, fees, bills or opportunity costs. Without a quantitative bound this is provisional prioritization, not a proven90%share.
policy: Prioritize targeted cases; resolve conditional cases with a brief specific question before opening a broader search.

For health-first cases skip broad survivor/lifetime-wage research unless direct comparative economic evidence emerges; retain a brief check for actual payments, benefits, caregiver/time burden, fines, payer/landlord incidence and overlap.
Do not invent arbitrary savings or costs simply to populate an income field. Zero/unknown economic effects are not proof of irrelevance; document the basis and limitations.
If materiality cannot be bounded cheaply, promote rather than declaring90%health. Do not force numerical changes or favorable estimates.

A screened report can retain its health-only price after an evidenced no-material-income disposition; acceptance/published x/15 counters advance only after independent disposition and verification, never from this triage alone.
